Katanga Mining Ltd Reports Steady Output as Copper Demand Holds Firm

Katanga Mining Ltd, a leading producer in the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) copper and cobalt sector, has published its routine quarterly production figures, indicating stable operations and output in the second quarter of 2024. The company reported copper cathode production of 67,500 tonnes, aligning closely with the previous quarter and reflecting consistent plant performance at its Kolwezi complex.

Cobalt output for the period reached 6,150 tonnes, a modest increase from the 6,020 tonnes recorded in the first quarter, as process optimisations introduced earlier this year continued to bear fruit. “The incremental improvements we’re seeing reflect our ongoing investment in efficiency and safety,” said Pascal Mbuyu, Katanga Mining Ltd’s operations manager. “The market remains robust, and we are committed to supplying our customers reliably.”

Export volumes remained stable, with the majority of shipments destined for Asia and Europe. According to the Congolese Chamber of Mines, the DRC’s copper exports remain a crucial contributor to national revenue. “Routine figures such as those from Katanga show the sector’s maturity and resilience,” commented Chamber spokesperson Clarisse Tshisekedi.

No major interruptions were reported during the quarter. Local union representatives described labour relations at the site as “constructive,” with routine safety training and health monitoring ongoing. “We are pleased with the regular dialogue between management and workers,” said Jean-Paul Kalemba, a union delegate at the Kolwezi plant.

Analysts at Kinshasa-based CopperMark Consulting noted that Katanga Mining Ltd’s stable output comes amid steady global demand for copper, supported by growth in the renewable energy and electronics sectors. “Katanga’s performance is a bellwether for mining operations in the region,” said analyst Roger Masiala. “Their consistency is positive for both local communities and international markets.”

Katanga Mining Ltd is expected to release its next production update in October.
